products.orange: Node.js runtime with workerd-shaped globals, cloudflare:* and node:* modules
products.note: fetch, scheduled, and queue handlers run unchanged. Compatibility dates and flags are not applied.

products.orange: Rivet Actors with SQLite storage and alarms
products.note: WebSocket hibernation is emulated. After 10 idle seconds, Orange drops the object's instance and keeps the actor and its accepted WebSockets open. The next event builds a new instance, and an auto-response frame is answered without one. The actor sleeps only when it has no open accepted WebSocket. A class from another Worker (script_name) runs when that Worker is in the same orange dev session. Rivet's _rivet_ tables are reserved in the object's SQLite.

products.orange: Internal Rivet Actor per namespace
products.note: Strongly consistent, so reads never see stale values. cacheStatus is always null.

products.orange: Internal Rivet Actor per database, on the Durable Object SQL bridge
products.note: meta.rows_read counts returned rows, not scanned rows, and meta.rows_written misses index and trigger writes.

products.orange: Actor SQLite by default, or any S3-compatible store per bucket
products.note: Pick the backend with ORANGE_R2_<BUCKET>_S3_* variables. On the default backend, one Rivet Actor stores each bucket, so Rivet's storage limit for one actor bounds the bucket. SSE-C keys throw.

configure.purpose: S3-compatible endpoint. Setting it moves the bucket off actor SQLite. <BUCKET> is bucket_name in upper case.
Optional. The default is AWS_REGION, then auto.

products.orange: Internal Rivet Actor per queue, delivered to the Worker's queue() handler
products.note: Queues are shared by name across an orange dev session, so a consumer in another Worker receives the messages. One batch at a time per queue.

products.orange: Cloudflare's own Workflows engine, copied from @cloudflare/workflows-shared 0.15.1, with one Rivet Actor per instance
products.note: create, get, status, sendEvent, steps, terminate, pause, resume, restart, and delete work, also with script_name across Workers in one session. terminate cannot stop a step callback that is already running.

products.orange: Internal Rivet Actor that evaluates the full Cloudflare cron syntax
products.note: Crons fire in orange dev, unlike wrangler dev. An overlapping run is skipped. A run has no 15 minute wall time limit.

products.orange: Internal Rivet Actor per namespace_id with an exact fixed-window counter
products.note: Counts are exact per window, while Cloudflare counts per location. Each limit() call is one actor round trip.

products.orange: Any OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenRouter by default, or ORANGE_AI_BASE_URL)
products.note: Text generation and embeddings run. The gateway option is accepted, but env.AI.gateway(), streaming inputs, and toMarkdown throw.

configure.purpose: Provider API key. OPENROUTER_API_KEY also works.
OpenAI-compatible base URL. The default is OpenRouter.
JSON map from @cf/ models to provider models, over the built-in map.

products.orange: Internal Rivet Actor per cache name, with Miniflare's freshness rules
products.note: Entries persist locally. Each key keeps one Vary variant, and several ranges return the whole body. ORANGE_CACHE=off gives the workers.dev no-op.

configure.purpose: Makes the Cache API the workers.dev no-op.

products.orange: A child Rivet Actor per facet
products.note: get, abort, delete, clone, and string IDs work, which covers the agents SDK.

products.orange: One Node.js process per dynamic Worker in an agentOS VM, never on the host, Workers RPC over Cap'n Web
products.note: get, load, fetch, and RPC work. getDurableObjectClass(), Python modules, and compiled Wasm modules throw.

products.orange: One runtime process per Worker in one orange dev session (orange dev -c a.jsonc -c b.jsonc), with fetch() and RPC over loopback HTTP
products.note: fetch(), JS RPC, and named entrypoints work. connect() to another Worker works; WebSocket upgrades to another Worker throw. Workers in separate orange dev processes do not find each other.

products.orange: env.DISPATCHER.get(name) finds the user Worker by name among the Workers of the orange dev session
products.note: Pass user Workers with more -c options. args, limits, and outbound Workers are ignored, and namespace membership is not checked.

products.orange: @cloudflare/sandbox on the ORANGE_SANDBOX_PROVIDER backend: a local host directory (default), an embedded agentOS VM through @rivet-dev/agentos-core, or E2B, Daytona, or Freestyle through @rivet-dev/sandbox-adapter
products.note: exec, files, processes, and preview URLs work. The image is ignored, and the local provider is not isolated. Sessions and the code interpreter throw, preview URLs need the local or agentOS provider, and agentOS VMs do not survive an orange dev restart.

configure.purpose: local (default), agentos, e2b, daytona, or freestyle.
Key for the chosen remote provider.
Optional. Where the local provider keeps sandbox directories.

products.orange: No container runtime. A class listed under containers gets a ctx.container that runs one sandbox per object on ORANGE_SANDBOX_PROVIDER
products.note: Images are not built or run, and start() takes only a Cloudflare Sandbox image (cloudflare/sandbox). start(), exec(), monitor(), destroy(), signal(), and getTcpPort().fetch() work. start({ entrypoint }), exec({ pty }), exec({ stdin }), the outbound HTTP intercepts, snapshotContainer(), and inspect() throw. ctx.container throws NotSupportedError in a class that containers does not list.

products.orange: Stub binding
products.note: Calls throw. Use a vector database over fetch(), or SQLite with cosine similarity for small sets.

products.orange: Your own headless Chrome or a hosted browser, through its DevTools Protocol endpoint
products.note: @cloudflare/puppeteer 1.x runs unchanged. With a browser you run, all sessions share it and its cookies; Browserbase starts a separate browser per session. browser.close() closes only the session's pages. keep_alive, location, and recording are ignored.

configure.purpose: The browser's DevTools endpoint, such as http://127.0.0.1:9222. Without it, calls throw an error that names it.

products.orange: Stub bindings
products.note: Calls throw. Use an image service such as imgproxy over fetch().

products.orange: Your SMTP server, with inbound email on /cdn-cgi/handler/email
products.note: send() takes an EmailMessage or a message object, with Cc, Bcc, and attachments, and enforces the address limits. A message POSTed to /cdn-cgi/handler/email runs email(), and forward() and reply() send over SMTP. Email Routing itself is Cloudflare-only, and Orange does not check sender domains.

configure.purpose: smtp:// (STARTTLS when offered) or smtps:// URL with the user name and password. Without it, send(), forward(), and reply() throw.
Bearer token or Basic auth password for the inbound route. orange serve needs it; orange dev checks it when it is set.

products.orange: Direct connection to the database in the connection string
products.note: Connects directly; no pooling or query cache

products.note: writeDataPoint() succeeds and stores nothing. There is no SQL API to query.
